662.t: Recordings: Marie Laveau for Joe Mares and other sessions
662.s: After rejoining in 1953 she recorded Marie Laveau with Papa's band for Joe Mares and did other sessions; the big band made no records, only the eight-piece band earlier.
662.q: No, we didn't do any recording with the big band. We did the recording when we had the eight piece band. The eight piece band. And then in later years, after I rejoined Papa's house then, around 53, we made this record for Merez. But during the time that we had the 14 piece band, we didn't do any…

962.t: Recording 'Healing Time' live with her band
962.s: Recorded largely live in New Orleans with her band and producer Mark Howard; first album written with the band, honoring drummer Samantha Banks.
962.q: Yeah, you know actually I don’t — this last CD that I did, “Healing Time” is recorded with my band and we did record live for the most part. Yeah. Come to think of it, as far as the rhythm section yeah, we definitely did play live for “Healing Time.” And looking back I played live for the most part…

329.s: Hanna's own album, unrehearsed, with Carmen Leggio, Danny Stiles, Mike Moore and John Bunch.
329.q: Yeah I did. One was a mistake. That was called “Jake Takes Manhattan” and it was supposed to be with Rosemary Clooney, although she didn’t show she got sick. And so we just put it together as an album. It was all off the top of my head. We never rehearsed a note. But we did it as we went along.…

563.t: Chapter One and Chapter Two sessions
563.s: Both albums were done in two sessions of five or six hours, using friends who had not necessarily played together.
563.q: Yeah. Two sessions. That was called “Chapter One,” we did that in two, I guess five hour sessions, maybe six hours on one of them; and then the second one is called “Chapter Two” — surprise, surprise — the plot thickens. And that was about the same, I think maybe two six hour sessions, two…

334.t: Recording the Jazz Party CD with Bill Berry in Los Angeles
334.s: He arranged a one-day Los Angeles session with Berry, Hanna, Brown and others, and wrote the title tune.
334.q: Oh here in Los Angeles. With Jake Hanna and Ray Brown. And a young tenor saxophonist, Sam Sadigursky. He was 19 years old. He is very good on tenor saxophone.

511.t: Making 'Sacred Hearts' with his Paris quartet
511.s: All original music recorded with his quartet in four days, overdubbed over four years, with no outside producer.
511.q: All original material, yeah. So the nucleus, the quartet on that record is the quartet that I work with here in Paris, and actually the drummer is one of my oldest friends from New Orleans named Jeff Boudreaux, who was in Paris before I was, also the bass player named Peter Giron is from New York…

494.t: Autumn in New York and Scratch with Holland and Humair
494.s: Uptown trio record, then Enja's Scratch, a first-meeting session that won a Paris award.
494.ch: Recordings as a leader and the Getz years
494.q: For Enja. No, that one wasn’t leased. That was their – that was the company. That was their suggestion, to do that. I had never met Dave or Daniel before the studio. So there was no rehearsal or anything with that. I brought some music, and Dave had a tune. That’s basically it. We just played. It…

372.s: Konitz says Giuffre created the album; he picked Marsh and Brown, and not the rhythm section.
372.q: I think Norman Granz had some suggestion about that. That’s all I really know about that. Jimmy suggested it and created it basically.

508.t: The last Kenny Kirkland session and the Requiem record
508.s: The record began as a studio rehearsal, and Kirkland died before the band could return to record it properly.
508.ch: Kenny Kirkland, Wynton's quintet and the jazz business
508.q: That record was tough, because it really wasn’t a record. See Kenny and Tain, you couldn’t get them to rehearse. If you called a rehearsal, they wouldn’t even show up. So, I said “OK.” So, I was on Columbia, so I’ll just use the power of a company like that and I’d call a recording session. And the…

388.t: The first Decca date and the series of albums
388.s: The first album with 'Jump for Joy' and 'Kisses and Jubilation' pleased Milt Gabler and began a series of twenty to thirty albums.
388.q: To sum it up better, that was the begining of a beautiful thing --' recording wise and friendship wise, and a series of albums, running between 20 and 30. We made in the middle twenties, amoung of albums.
